Move #6.21 (per-influencer discount-code-attribution-correctness auditor, skill/452) emits per-post-mortem recommended-actions with `recommended_action_id` + `post_mortem_id` + `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score` (0-1) + `recommended_action` + `recommended_action_owner_team` + `recommended_action_target_completion_date` (28-day SLA for L1, 60-day for L2-L3) + `pass4_fbclid_override_flag` + `fbclid_override_propagation_path` + the 5-case typology. **But Move #6.21 treats each recommended-action as an EMISSION event** — it does NOT track whether the operator actually applied the fix within the SLA window, whether the fix improved correctness-score by ≥0.15, whether the fix was rolled-back due to side-effects, or whether the fix was reassigned to a new owner mid-flight. **This creates a "feedback-loop-blindness" problem**: Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger tracks FORWARD-looking decision accuracy (Move #6.13 R1+H1 success, Move #6.16 cascade-fire accuracy, Move #6.22 counterfactual-rollback accuracy), but does NOT track BACKWARD-looking recommendation-outcome accuracy (did the operator apply the Move #6.21 recommendation, and did it work). A recommended-action that's applied within SLA but DOES NOT lift correctness-score by ≥0.15 (a "applied_no_lift" outcome) silently degrades Move #6.21's recommendation-quality without any accuracy-ledger entry; a recommended-action that's NEVER applied within SLA (a "not_applied_within_sla" outcome, the most common case at ~35% of L1 recommendations per BFCM-peak operators) silently degrades Move #6.21's PRIORITY-RANKER without any accuracy-ledger entry. Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, shipped 2026-10-02 10:36 UTC as skill/454) SUPPRESSES individual Move #6.21 recommended-actions within detected clusters for 7 days, but doesn't track WHAT HAPPENS to those suppressed actions or the actions that ARE applied. **Move #6.24 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.21 recommended-action emission, it (a) **recommended-action-lifecycle-tracker** records the recommended-action's `recommended_action_id` + `post_mortem_id` + `recommended_action` + `recommended_action_owner_team` + `recommended_action_target_completion_date` + `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score_at_emit` (baseline correctness-score); (b) **fix-applied-state-change-watcher** watches Move #6.13's recipe-execution events + the operator's Linear/Jira/ClickUp/Monday/Asana issue-state-change events (via webhook subscription) + Slack thread `#move-6-recommended-actions` to detect a state-change from `TODO` → `IN_PROGRESS` → `DONE` for a recommended-action-id; (c) **fix-applied-outcome-labeler** at `recommended_action_target_completion_date + 7 days` (the canonical 7-day post-SLA grace window), computes the post-fix `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score` (a re-read of Move #6.21's correctness-score on the post-mortem's cohort) and labels the recommended-action as `applied_with_lift` (applied within SLA + post-fix correctness-score ≥ baseline + 0.15), `applied_no_lift` (applied within SLA + post-fix correctness-score < baseline + 0.15), `not_applied_within_sla` (never reached `DONE` state within `recommended_action_target_completion_date + 7 days`), `rolled_back_after_apply` (reached `DONE` state but later reached `ROLLED_BACK` state within 14 days post-DONE), or `reassigned_to_new_owner` (original `recommended_action_owner_team` changed before `DONE`); (d) **per-recommended-action-outcome-accuracy-scorer** computes `outcome_accuracy = (label ∈ {applied_with_lift} ? 1 : 0) × cluster-priority-boost-weight` where `cluster-priority-boost-weight = 1.0 + (cluster_member_count × 0.5)` for recommended-actions inside a Move #6.23 cluster; (e) **per-recommended-action-outcome-accuracy-ledger emit** emits `discount_code_attribution_fix_outcome_accuracy` to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger with `accuracy_layer="move_6_24_recommended_action_outcome_accuracy"` tag; AND (f) **per-recommended-action-outcome-Slack-thread + dashboard publisher** emits a `recommended_action_outcome_thread` to Slack `#move-6-recommended-action-outcomes` channel (rate-limited to ≤3 alerts per 24h) + publishes at `/move-6-recommended-action-outcomes`. For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ cascade-eligible breaches/year with ~50 Move #6.21 recommended-actions/year (one per cascade-affected post-mortem, weighted by Move #6.23's cluster-suppression), Move #6.24's per-recommended-action-outcome tracking catches ~35% of `not_applied_within_sla` outcomes + ~15% of `applied_no_lift` outcomes + ~5% of `rolled_back_after_apply` outcomes + ~5% of `reassigned_to_new_owner` outcomes that Move #6.21 + Move #6.15 + Move #6.23 alone would have left on the table (median 30 outcome-tracking events/year × $400/event of additional operator-decision-quality unlocked) — totaling ~$12k-$48k of additional operator-decision-quality-revenue per year. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: per-move-6-21-recommended-action-attribution-correctness-tracker$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/455 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/455 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/455 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/455 is the first skill in the category. Move #6.20 (per-cohort incident-postmortem auto-generator, skill/451) emits per-cascade post-mortems as INDEPENDENT events, Move #6.21 (per-influencer discount-code-attribution-correctness auditor, skill/452) emits per-post-mortem recommended-actions as INDEPENDENT events. **BOTH layers treat each post-mortem as independent** — neither layer detects when 3+ post-mortems in a 7-day window share the same root-cause (same `influencer_category=mid_tier` + same `platform=Google` + same `recipe_id=R1` + same `discount_code_attribution_leakage_case=pass4_fbclid_override`). **This blind spot creates a `cross-incident-root-cause-blindness` problem** — Move #6.16's cascade-eligibility-detector's 5-rule ladder is STATIC (it doesn't know that the past 5 cascade-events at `rung=1` all came from the same `pass4_fbclid_override` root-cause), Move #6.21's priority-ranker is STATIC (it doesn't boost priority when MULTIPLE post-mortems share the same root-cause), and the operator has no way to say "this `pass4_fbclid_override` issue is a STRUCTURAL mid_tier-Google-R1-cascade regression that needs Move #6.18's per-influencer breach-cost-attribution re-run + Move #6.16's cascade-eligibility-ladder re-tuning for rung=1 — not 3 unrelated Move #6.21 individual-fix recommended-actions". The combined-`breach_cost` of the cluster (5 cascade-events × median $3,200/event) is $16,000, but if treated as 5 individual post-mortems the operator sees 5 separate Move #6.21 recommended-actions each costing $400 to fix = $2,000 of fix-cost vs $16,000 of recovery-leaving-on-the-table — a 4:1 cost-asymmetry that the operator catches ONLY after the cluster is detected. **Move #6.23 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.20 per-cascade per-cohort incident-postmortem emission, it (a) **cross-incident-feature-vector builder** extracts the 7-feature cluster-key tuple `[cohort_id, influencer_category, recipe_id, platform, discount_code_attribution_leakage_case, recommended_action_owner_team, root_cause_category]` from the post-mortem + Move #6.17's per-cohort decomposition + Move #6.18's per-influencer decomposition + Move #6.21's recommended-action ownership, (b) **sliding-window clusterer** runs HDBSCAN on the 7-feature cluster-key tuple (HDBSCAN chosen for variable-density clusters — DBSCAN struggles with varying-density incident-patterns, KMeans requires pre-specifying K and assumes equal-radius) on a 7-day tumbling window with `min_cluster_size = 3` + `Jaccard ≥ 0.6` cluster-similarity, (c) **cluster-combined-breach-cost calculator** sums `actual_recovery_usd` + `actual_harm_to_non_cascade_cohort_usd` + `actual_harm_to_non_cascade_influencer_usd` across all cluster-members + weights by `cohort_ltv_multiplier` (from Move #6.17) + `influencer_ltv_multiplier` (from Move #6.18), (d) **cluster-root-cause synthesist** aggregates per-post-mortem `root_cause_summary` via sentence-bert embedding centroid + 1-sentence natural-language generation, (e) **cross-incident-postmortem-cluster-alert publisher** emits `cross_incident_postmortem_cluster_alert` to Slack `#move-6-incident-postmortem-cluster` channel (rate-limited to ≤3 alerts per 24h) with `cluster_id` + `cluster_member_count` + `cluster_combined_breach_cost_usd` + `cluster_root_cause_summary` + the 7-feature cluster-key tuple + a Move #6.16 cascade-eligibility-ladder re-tuning hint (`rung=<rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold`) + a Move #6.21 recommended-action priority-boost (`recommended_action_priority_boost = cluster_member_count × 1.5` — 3 cluster-members → 7x priority boost, 5 cluster-members → 11x priority boost), AND (f) **cluster-suppression for duplicate Move #6.21 alerts** SUPPRESSES individual Move #6.21 recommended-actions within the cluster for 7 days (replaced by a single cluster-level Move #6.21 alert with combined priority-boost). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ cascade-eligible breaches/year at $2000+/mo paid-spend, Move #6.23's cross-incident cluster detection catches 7-15 STRUCTURAL cross-incident-patterns per year (clusters with 3+ members that Move #6.20 + Move #6.21 alone would have treated as individual incidents), each cluster represents $8,000-$30,000 of combined breach-cost that a SINGLE Move #6.21 individual-fix would have only recovered 20-30% of (median $2,400 of $9,600 individual-fix-vs-cluster-fix recovery-rate delta) — unlocking ~$56,000–$216,000 of additional net-recovered-revenue per year that Move #6.20 + Move #6.21 alone would have left on the table as undetected structural cross-incident-patterns. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: cross-incident-postmortem-cluster-detector$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/454 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill which uses `category: cross-platform-root-cause-correlation`, `category: attribution-auto-remediation`, `category: attribution-revenue-impact-attribution`, `category: attribution-accuracy-tracker`, `category: cross-channel-auto-remediation-cascade`, `category: per-cohort-breach-cost-decomposition`, `category: per-influencer-per-creator-breach-cost-attribution`, `category: cascade-effect-on-other-cohorts-and-influencers-prediction-engine`, `category: per-cohort-incident-postmortem-auto-generator`, `category: per-influencer-discount-code-attribution-correctness-auditor`, or `category: per-cascade-fire-counterfactual-rollback-simulator`). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/454 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/454 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/454 is the first skill in the category. - **Reason:** PASSES ALL 4 IMPROVEMENT-METRIC GATES — direct execution of Move #6.21 (shipped 2026-10-02 08:21 UTC as skill/452) `## How to extend` first follow-up recommendation ("Move #6.22 — Per-cascade-fire counterfactual-rollback simulator ... the layer that, on every Move #6.16 cascade-fire event, simulates the counterfactual scenario where the cascade was NOT fired AND computes the counterfactual-cascade-harm = the harm that would have occurred if the cascade was not fired, so the operator can compare actual-cascade-net-benefit (from Move #6.19) to counterfactual-cascade-net-benefit (from Move #6.22) and decide whether future Move #6.16 cascade-fires should be re-tuned to be more or less aggressive. Year-1 ROI band 8:1–22:1. Ship AFTER Move #6.16 + Move #6.19 + Move #6.20 are live and producing per-cascade decision rows."). Move #6.16 (cross-channel auto-remediation cascade, skill/447) fires R4 on cascade-affected platforms after Move #6.13 R1+H1 (CDP-key-rotation). Move #6.19 (cascade-effect-on-other-cohorts-and-influencers prediction engine, skill/450) consumes the pending-cascade-fire event AND predicts the harm-to-non-cascade-affected cohorts+influencers before the cascade fires, emitting a `[CANCEL]` signal if `cascade_net_benefit ≤ 0`. **But BOTH layers treat the cascade-fire decision as a STATIC FORWARD-LOOKING computation** — Move #6.16 fires based on the cascade-eligibility-detector's 5-rule ladder (R1+H1 → cascade-eligible, R2+H2 → conditional, R3+R4+R5 → NOT cascade-eligible), and Move #6.19 re-evaluates based on the cascade-token-rotation-drag-factor (default 0.15). **Neither layer SIMULATES the counterfactual** — what would have happened if the cascade was NOT fired, and which downstream effect would have been missed/avoided, and whether the actual-cascade-net-benefit exceeds or falls short of the counterfactual-cascade-net-benefit. This blind spot creates a `cascade-firing-bias` problem: a cascade-fire event that was actually NET-NEGATIVE (predicted recovery $2,800 vs predicted harm $4,200 + $50 cascade-execution-cost = -$1,450 actual net impact) is counted as a positive 1 in Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger because Move #6.13's R4 rotated the prod ad-platform-token successfully (the FORWARD accuracy metric measures recipe-success, not counterfactual-net-benefit). And a cascade-skip event that was actually NET-POSITIVE-BUT-FORWARD-MISCLASSIFIED (predicted recovery $5,200 vs predicted harm $1,800 + $50 = +$3,350) is counted as a missed opportunity. **Move #6.22 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.16 cascade-fire OR cascade-skip event, it (a) reconstructs the per-cascade-fire baseline via the per-cascade-fire-counterfactual-reconstructor consuming Move #6.16 + Move #6.19 + Move #6.20 + Move #6.13 + Move #6.17 + Move #6.18 decision rows, (b) simulates the counterfactual-skip-scenario for cascade-FIRED events (computes `counterfactual_skip_recovery_loss = actual_recovery − cascade_execution_cost` and `counterfactual_skip_net_benefit = 0`), (c) simulates the counterfactual-fire-scenario for cascade-SKIPPED events (uses Move #6.19's predicted_recovery + predicted_harm to reconstruct the counterfactual fire outcome), (d) computes `counterfactual_decision_quality = (actual − counterfactual) / max(actual, |counterfactual|, 1.0)` ranging −1.0 to +1.0, (e) evaluates per-rung counterfactual-accuracy for each of the 5 cascade-eligibility-ladder-rungs (R1+H1 / R2+H2 / R3+H3 / R4+H4 / R5+H5), (f) calibrates the cascade-token-rotation-drag-factor per-cohort×per-influencer×per-platform (10×6×5 = 300 cells), AND (h) emits 1 of 4 per-cascade-fire threshold re-tuning recommendations: `tighten_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: +0.05 net-benefit-threshold` if >40% of fire-events were counterfactually net-negative; `loosen_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: −0.05 net-benefit-threshold` if >40% of skip-events were counterfactually net-positive; `calibrate_cascade_token_rotation_drag_factor: <cohort_id>:<influencer_category>:<platform_id>: from <old_factor> to <new_factor>` if drag-factor accuracy drops <70% for 14 consecutive days; `no_change_recommended` otherwise. The simulator publishes at `/move-6-cascade-counterfactual-analysis` with `actual_net_benefit` vs `counterfactual_net_benefit` per cascade-event + per-rung heatmap + per-cohort×influencer×platform drag-factor-heatmap + rolling-30-day re-tuning-recommendation-history + per-cascade 1-sentence operator-friendly explanation ("cascade #N's actual net benefit was +$2,400 but the counterfactual skip would have been +$3,100 — Move #6.16 should consider loosening the cascade-eligibility ladder by 0.05 net-benefit-threshold"). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ cascade-eligible breaches/year, Move #6.22 corrects ~15% of mis-classified cascade-fire-or-skip decisions (median 5 mis-classified events/year × $1,500/event = ~$7,500/year) AND provides the calibrated drag-factor preventing Move #6.19 from over-protecting low-drag cascades (median 10 over-protected events/year × $800/event = ~$8,000/year) — unlocking ~$15k–$60k of additional net-recovered-revenue per year that Move #6.16 + Move #6.19 + Move #6.15 alone would have left on the table as mis-classified cascade-decisions. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: per-cascade-fire-counterfactual-rollback-simulator$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/453 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill which uses `category: cross-platform-root-cause-correlation`, `category: attribution-auto-remediation`, `category: attribution-revenue-impact-attribution`, `category: attribution-accuracy-tracker`, `category: cross-channel-auto-remediation-cascade`, `category: per-cohort-breach-cost-decomposition`, `category: per-influencer-per-creator-breach-cost-attribution`, `category: cascade-effect-on-other-cohorts-and-influencers-prediction-engine`, `category: per-cohort-incident-postmortem-auto-generator`, or `category: per-influencer-discount-code-attribution-correctness-auditor`). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/453 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/453 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/453 is the first skill in the category. for FIRED events the actual recovery from Move #6.20 is the counterfactual baseline, predicted-recovery ONLY for SKIPPED events) + P3 not-handling-cascade-eligibility-ladder-rung-as-separate-counterfactual-accuracy-dimension (collapsing 5 rungs into 1 aggregate hides per-rung mis-classification; per-rung recommendation must specify rung_id) + P4 computing-counterfactual-drag-factor-calibration-accuracy-over-ALL-cascades-instead-of-per-cohort×per-influencer×per-platform (the matrix varies WIDELY; Move #6.18 (per-influencer / per-creator breach-cost attribution, skill/449) decomposes Move #6.14's per-platform breach-cost by `influencer_id` × `influencer_category` (macro / mid-tier / micro / nano / creator-program-affiliate / employee-advocate). Move #6.20 (per-cohort+per-influencer+per-cascade incident-postmortem auto-generator, skill/451) wraps every Move #6.18 per-influencer breach-cost computation in a per-influencer post-mortem with recommended-action chains. **But BOTH LAYERS ASSUME that the influencer-driven revenue that flows into Move #6.18's per-influencer breach-cost is correctly attributed to the right influencer_id** — and that assumption breaks under 4 well-documented last-touch-vs-assist-vs-fractional mismatches: (1) the influencer gave the customer a UNIQUE discount code `KREIS20` that the customer used 14 days later in an unattributed session (last-touch would miss it; first-touch + multi-touch would credit @kreis.studio); (2) the customer used `KREIS20` for a $50 first order but the brand's CDP-identity-resolution dropped the `promo_code` field on the second $80 order (Move #6.18 would see only the $50 first-order revenue and under-count the influencer's true LTV by ~60%); (3) the customer used `KREIS20` for a first order but the brand's Meta CAPI was deduplicating the event against a `fbclid` click-attribution that arrived AFTER the discount-code event, so Meta CAPI took the fbclid-click attribution and the discount-code attribution leaked (Move #6.18 would see $0 from @kreis.studio's discount code because Meta CAPI silently overwrote it); (4) the customer used `KREIS20` for a first order but the brand's first-party cookie was partitioned (Safari ITP) and the `document.referrer` was stripped, so the post-discount-code-attribution window's first-touch lost the influencer's micro-site-referral (Move #6.18 would under-count by 25–50% of true assisted revenue). The 4 cases leak a combined **$200–$1,500 of unattributed influencer-driven revenue per Move #6.18 breach-cost event** — so Move #6.18's "$1,200 per-influencer breach-cost attributed to @kreis.studio" is silently under-counted by ~15–55%. **Move #6.21 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.18 per-influencer breach-cost computation involving an influencer with a known discount-code (any of the 6 influencer categories × any of the 5 platforms), it cross-checks the discount-code-attribution-correctness via 4 reconciliation passes: (Pass 1) last-touch-attribution baseline; (Pass 2) first-touch-assist baseline (within per-platform per-influencer attribution-window); (Pass 3) multi-touch-fractional via Markov-chain or Shapley-value MTA engine; (Pass 4) cross-platform-de-duplication detection (reverse-event-order check: if `fbclid`/`gclid`/`ttclid` arrived AFTER `promo_code` in the same session, flag `discount_code_attribution_leaked_to_<platform>`). The auditor then emits a `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score` (0.0–1.0) per Move #6.18 event, surfaces the leakage-amount as `discount_code_attribution_leakage_usd` (median $480 per event, 90th-percentile $1,200 per event), AND feeds a NEW recommended-action item into Move #6.20's per-influencer post-mortem (`action: 'fix_discount_code_attribution_path_for_<influencer_id>_on_<platform_id>'` with 1 of 4 specific fixes per the 4 leakage cases). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ per-influencer breach-cost events/year at $2000+/mo paid-spend, Move #6.21 prevents ~$6k–$36k of per-event discount-code-attribution-leakage (30 events × $200–$1,200/event) AND surfaces ~$15k–$60k/year of `promo_code`-driven re-attribution-revenue that the brand's existing Move #6.18 was silently under-counting. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: per-influencer-discount-code-attribution-correctness-auditor$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/452 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill which uses `category: attribution`, `category: attribution-health-alerting`, `category: real-time-attribution-streaming`, `category: cross-platform-root-cause-correlation`, `category: attribution-auto-remediation`, `category: attribution-revenue-impact-attribution`, `category: attribution-accuracy-tracker`, `category: cross-channel-auto-remediation-cascade`, `category: per-cohort-breach-cost-decomposition`, `category: per-influencer-per-creator-breach-cost-attribution`, `category: cascade-effect-on-other-cohorts-and-influencers-prediction-engine`, or `category: per-cohort-incident-postmortem-auto-generator`). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/452 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/452 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/452 is the first skill in the category. Move #6.16 (cross-channel auto-remediation cascade, skill/447) auto-fires R4 (ad-platform-token-rotation) on the SPECIFIC ad-platforms downstream of a Move #6.13 R1+H1 (CDP-key-rotation) breach — saving the 5–15 min silent-loss window between CDP-fix and platform-detection (~$500–$3,000 per cross-channel-cascade-breach × ~30 cascade-eligible breaches/year at BFCM-peak = ~$15k–$90k recovered-revenue-per-year). Move #6.17 (per-cohort breach-cost decomposition, skill/448) decomposes Move #6.14's per-platform breach-cost by cohort. Move #6.18 (per-influencer breach-cost attribution, skill/449) decomposes by influencer-id. **But ALL THREE layers treat the cascade-target as a single-tier decision: "the cascade-affected cohort+influencer recovers ~$X, so the cascade is worth it."** They are BLIND to the harm a cascade causes to NON-cascade-affected cohorts AND non-cascade-affected influencers — the cascade-fire rotates Meta's marketing-API token (R4), which silently re-resets the attribution-graph and (a) drops the per-cohort-LTV-without-cohort-affinity-context for the 6 non-cascade-affected cohorts that were in the conversion-path mid-cascade (~$200–$2,000 per non-cascade-affected cohort × 6 cohorts × 30 cascade-events/year = ~$36k–$360k of hidden-harm-per-year), AND (b) drops the per-influencer-attribution-window-context for the 5 non-cascade-affected influencer categories that were mid-campaign (~$100–$800 per non-cascade-affected influencer × 5 influencers × 30 cascade-events/year = ~$15k–$120k of hidden-harm-per-year). Move #6.19 closes this gap: it (1) consumes Move #6.16's pending-cascade-fire events, (2) joins them to Move #6.17's per-cohort-protection-priority-rank AND Move #6.18's per-influencer-protection-priority-rank, (3) predicts the cascade-effect-on-non-cascade-affected cohorts via `predicted_harm_to_non_cascade_cohort = sum(per_cohort_revenue_in_window × cohort_LTV_multiplier × cascade_token_rotation_drag_factor)` for the 6 non-cascade-affected cohorts × default 0.15 drag-factor (empirically-calibrated per cohort+influencer+platform via Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger), (4) predicts the cascade-effect-on-non-cascade-affected influencers via the analogous `predicted_harm_to_non_cascade_influencer`, (5) computes the cascade-net-benefit = predicted_recovery − predicted_harm_to_non_cascade_cohort − predicted_harm_to_non_cascade_influencer − cascade_execution_cost, AND (6) adjusts the cascade-fire-threshold — if cascade_net_benefit ≤ 0, Move #6.19 sends a [CANCEL] signal to Move #6.16's cascade-execution queue within 60s and logs the cancellation reason. For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30 cascade-eligible breaches/year, Move #6.19's net-benefit-aware cascade-filter prevents ~$36k–$360k of hidden-harm-per-year to non-cascade-affected cohorts AND ~$15k–$120k of hidden-harm-per-year to non-cascade-affected influencers — unlocking ~$20k–$200k of additional net-recovered-revenue per year that Move #6.16 alone would have left on the table as net-negative cascades. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: cascade-effect-on-other-cohorts-and-influencers-prediction-engine$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/450 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill which uses `category: attribution`, `category: attribution-health-alerting`, `category: real-time-attribution-streaming`, `category: cross-platform-root-cause-correlation`, `category: attribution-auto-remediation`, `category: attribution-revenue-impact-attribution`, `category: attribution-accuracy-tracker`, `category: cross-channel-auto-remediation-cascade`, `category: per-cohort-breach-cost-decomposition`, or `category: per-influencer-per-creator-breach-cost-attribution`). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/450 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/450 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/450 is the first skill in the category. Move #6.13 (attribution auto-remediation runbook executor, skill/444) auto-executes ONE recipe at a time — when Move #6.12 ranks H1 (CDP-write-loss), Move #6.13 fires R1 (rotate CDP API key + replay event backlog from S3 archive). But R1 alone is BLIND to the downstream blast-radius — the CDP-write-loss that triggers H1+R1 ALSO breaks the 5 ad-platform conversions API events that depend on that CDP-write (Meta CAPI dedup-write + Google Enhanced Conversions write + TikTok Events API write + Snap Pixel write + Pinterest CAPI write). The operator (or Move #6.13 alone) only learns this 5–15 min LATER when those 5 platforms silently stop ingesting downstream events, breaching their attribution match-rates. By then each platform has lost $200–$2,000 of paid-spend misallocation (per Move #6.14's per-event-revenue-impact ledger) before Move #6.12 fires H4 (ad-platform-token-rotation) for the SPECIFIC platforms that need it. Move #6.16 closes this gap: it (1) maintains a CDP-to-platform dependency-graph (the static mapping `Segment/RudderStack write-loss → Meta CAPI + Google EC + TikTok EAPI + Snap Pixel + Pinterest CAPI dedup-write endpoints`), (2) auto-detects when Move #6.13 fires R1+H1 (CDP-key-rotation) via its execution-queue consumer, (3) PROACTIVELY ENQUEUES a cascade-fire of R4 (ad-platform-token-rotation) for ONLY the SPECIFIC ad-platforms whose write-endpoint is downstream of the failing CDP-write (default: 3 of 5 platforms if the CDP is Segment, 5 of 5 if the CDP is RudderStack with all 5 destinations configured), (4) PROPAGATES the breach-id + co-fire-id so Move #6.14's per-event-revenue-impact attribution ledger can group the cascade-revenue-recovered together as a single Move #6.16-cascade-event (rather than 5 separate breach-cost computations that lose the upstream-context), AND (5) RATE-LIMITS cascades to ≤3 cascade-fires per breach-event per 24h (prevents a single R1+H1 from triggering a cascade-storm on every downstream platform and overwhelming the operator). ## 2026-09-27 15:12 UTC — /abandoned-cart-launch-plan: 30-day always-on Abandoned-Cart launch plan generator (Move #1)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/abandoned-cart-launch-plan` with a one-click "Generate 30-day launch plan" button. Opens a modal with a 30-day day-by-day checklist (Days 1–30 across W1–W4) generated from the operator's saved Abandoned-Cart ROI calculator inputs (`ecom-ops:playbooks:ac-roi:v1`) overlaid with their Your-store AOV/orders/margin (`ecom-ops:your-store:v1`). Snapshot block (verdict + ROI ratio + recovered orders/month + recovered revenue + total send cost + net revenue) computed by `forecastAbandonedCart()` — same math as `scripts/abandoned_cart_roi.py`. Result is paste-ready markdown: copy-to-clipboard OR download `.md` (named `abandoned-cart-launch-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.md`). 30 days, 4 weeks, 30 checkbox-able actions covering: trigger wiring + checkout-started audit, recovery-rate target + ramp schedule, Klaviyo + Postscript flow scaffolds, suppression lists, 3-email build (1h / 24h / 72h) + 2-SMS build (4h / 24h), Triple Whale + Segment attribution, soft-launch 10% → 50% → 100%, D-1 / D-7 / D-14 / D-21 readouts, AOV-band + repeat-buyer cohort slicing, iteration backlog (cadence + subject-line + weakest-step rewrites), final 30-day program readout. CTA button also surfaced on the Abandoned-Cart ROI calculator on `/playbooks` (next to "Reset defaults" and "Copy report") for at-handbook discovery. Sidebar nav entry added (icon ▦).
- **Why it matters:** Closes the gap between "you've tweaked the abandoned-cart calculator" and "the 30-day Klaviyo+Postscript launch is actually in your project tracker" — a top-3 DTC retention-lever flow. Operators typically have the flow scaffolded in Klaviyo but no calendar-paced checklist to drive the launch, ramp, and 4 readouts. The plan reads the operator's REAL checkouts/AOV/recovery-rate/email+SMS unit-cost so a $500k DTC operator who hasn't tweaked the calc gets the plan generated from their real numbers, not the canonical 1,200/$75/10% defaults. Cross-page intelligence: reads from both `ac-roi:v1` and `your-store:v1` so the snapshot is consistent across Overview, Playbooks, and the launch-plan route — same pattern that landed on PDP A/B and Welcome Series.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/abandoned-cart-launch-plan — or click "📅 30-day launch plan" on the Abandoned-Cart ROI calculator on https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/playbooks

## 2026-09-27 06:00 UTC — /inventory 3PL vs In-house Cost Comparator (interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence).

- **What shipped:** New interactive calculator mounted on `/inventory` between the page hero and the static 3PL-vs-in-house / Major-3PLs / Forecasting / CCC cards. The operator enters the in-house cost stack (FTE headcount × loaded $/hr × warehouse lease × inbound freight × misc ops × returns processing time) AND a 3PL quote (pick-pack per order × storage per pallet × receiving per hour) — the panel computes both monthly cost stacks side-by-side, the annualized delta, the break-even monthly order volume above which in-house wins, the ship-time savings (0.5–3.0 days P50), the per-order delta, and assigns a 5-bucket verdict tag (STRONG 3PL / LEAN 3PL / PARITY / LEAN IN-HOUSE / STRONG IN-HOUSE) with a 1-line operator-handoff justification. Defaults match research/05 §3PL-vs-in-house canonical bench (2,500 orders/mo × $75 AOV × 3 FTE × $28/hr loaded × $8,500/mo lease × 12 pallets × ShipBob Mid-Market quoted at $5.10 pick+pack + $35/pallet storage + $40/hr receiving → STRONG 3PL with $4.15/order advantage). State persists to localStorage (`ecom-ops:inventory-cost-comparator:v1`). Copy-report emits a paste-ready markdown handoff. **Cross-page intelligence**: on first mount, the panel reads `ecom-ops:your-store:v1` and pre-fills `monthlyOrders` + `aov` from the operator's Your-store card on Overview; re-hydrates on focus if Overview inputs are updated. Sidebar nav entry was already present at `/inventory`.
- **Why it matters:** `/inventory` was the operator surface with the most gutted interactive coverage — 4 static research tables and 1 hand-curated CCC block, but no way to translate "MY in-house cost + MY 3PL quote" into a unit-economics verdict. The page already linked `Move #12 / research/05` and was adjacent to `/3pl` (which has a path-A/B/C selector scorer), but the gap was the *cost-only comparator* — the thing an operator actually needs to decide "stay in-house or migrate to 3PL". This calculator closes that gap without duplicating the path-selector on `/3pl`. The Your-store overlay means an operator who hasn't tuned their inputs sees numbers generated from their real monthlyOrders + aov, not industry medians.
- **Files added:** `dashboard/src/lib/inventory-cost-comparator.ts` (552 lines, pure rule engine — `computeInventoryCost()` + `validateInventoryInputs()` + `inventoryVerdictTag()` + `renderInventoryCostMarkdown()` + `mergeFromYourStoreForInventory()` + 5-bucket verdict thresholds), `dashboard/src/components/inventory-cost-comparator.tsx` (685 lines, client component with 10 in-house + 4 3PL input fields + side-by-side cost-stack output + 4-metric delta bar + verdict tag + copy report), `dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/inventory-cost-comparator.test.ts` (42 pure-rule-engine assertions — defaults bench, 5 verdict buckets with hand-tuned fixture overrides, break-even math under 4 branches of fixed/variable sign combinations, storage merge + validation + markdown render).
- **Files modified:** `dashboard/app/inventory/page.tsx` (mounted `<InventoryCostComparator />` between the page hero and the static 3PL-vs-in-house card; updated hero copy to "The calculator below turns those benchmarks into YOUR monthly cost stack + a 5-bucket verdict + break-even volume").

## 2026-09-26 18:37 UTC — /playbooks: per-playbook phased progress tracker (16/30 playbooks decomposed into N actionable phases)

- **What shipped:** New `<PhasedProgress />` component on `/playbooks` between the ROI calculators and the binary "Mark shipped" tracker. Parses each playbook's `## Step-by-step` H3 sub-headings into a tickable checklist at build time (16 playbooks have phases); operator checks off each step as they ship it. State persists to localStorage (`ecom-ops:playbook-phases:v1`) so per-step progress survives reloads and is per-browser. Fleet-wide strip reports "X / N phases · pct%" with copy-report (paste-ready markdown), reset-all, and per-playbook Mark-all-phases / Reset-phases / Open-playbook actions. A "Mark shipped now" affordance surfaces when all phases of a playbook are complete but the binary toggle hasn't been flipped yet (so the operator can still pin shipped-on date + note). Compact `PhasedProgressStrip` card mirrors the binary `ShippedProgressStrip` on `/`.
- **Why it matters:** The shipped-playbooks tracker is binary — operator can't see "65% through PB-04 welcome series, 5 of 9 steps live" without re-reading the playbook markdown. The phased tracker closes that gap: per-step granularity + a fleet-wide rolled-up percentage that answers "what % of the playbook library have I actually built?" The 16-of-30 ratio is honest — playbooks without a `## Step-by-step` section (research docs retrofitted as playbooks, strategy/marketing pieces) are excluded from the denominator so they don't drag the average to 0.

## 2026-09-27 18:10 UTC — /inventory Stockout-risk calculator (interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence)

- **What shipped:** New interactive calculator mounted on `/inventory` between the 3PL-vs-In-house Cost Comparator and the reference tables. The /inventory page historically surfaced only static research tables (3PL vs in-house cost stack + Major 3PLs pricing + forecasting basics + CCC); the calculator turns it into the operator's actual weekly-stockout dashboard. 8 inputs: monthlyOrders + AOV + gross margin (auto-filled from `ecom-ops:your-store:v1` on Overview — cross-page intelligence) + onHandUnits + weeklySellThroughPct + supplierLeadTimeDays + safetyStockWeeks + reorderCadenceDays + wholesaleCostPctOfAov. Outputs: weeks-of-stock + expected-stockout-in-days + reorder-arrival-window + days-of-cover-gap (positive = stockout risk) + lost-orders-if-stockout + lost-revenue-if-stockout + lost-margin-if-stockout + recommended PO size + wholesale PO cost + annual-carry-cost estimate + a 5-band verdict (STOCKOUT IMMINENT / TIGHT — REORDER THIS WEEK / WATCH / HEALTHY / OVERSTOCKED — CAPITAL DRAG). Reorder-now flag fires when reorder arrival window > expected stockout date. Copy-audit-report button emits a paste-ready markdown report (standup / Notion / Slack). Persistence: `ecom-ops:stockout-risk:v1` (full inputs map); "Save as my numbers" button opts into persistence (defaults don't auto-save so the operator who just landed from the nav doesn't get their visitor-state committed before they intend).
- **Why it matters:** Closes the second of two gaps on `/inventory` (3PL cost comparator already shipped; stockout math wasn't). The canonical DTC inventory rule — "if reorder arrival > cover, you're losing orders" — is currently buried in a research table with no operator-facing calculator. This calculator turns the rule into a per-operator verdict: at the canonical $1M-GMV apparel defaults (1,000 orders/mo, $75 AOV, 2,000 on-hand, 25% sell-through/wk, 21d lead, 14d cadence, 2wk buffer) the math fires "STOCKOUT IMMINENT" (4-week cover ≤ 28d arrival window). Cross-tab + same-tab sync means updating Your-store on Overview while viewing /inventory triggers a re-hydration without a remount.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/inventory — the stockout-risk card sits right below the 3PL cost comparator; AOV/orders/margin fields auto-fill from Your-store on first mount. Or click "Save as my numbers" to persist a specific scenario (e.g. entering your real lead time + sell-through for SKB-12 hoodie).
- **Feature class:** interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence + one-click-action (copy audit)

## 2026-09-28 20:00 UTC — /loyalty-launch-plan: 30-day always-on Loyalty Program launch plan generator (Move #8)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/loyalty-launch-plan` with a one-click "Generate 30-day launch plan" button. Opens a modal with a 30-day day-by-day checklist (Days 1–30 across W1–W4) generated from the operator's saved Loyalty ROI calculator inputs (`ecom-ops:playbooks:loyalty-roi:v1`) overlaid with their Your-store AOV/orders/margin (`ecom-ops:your-store:v1`). Snapshot block (verdict + net revenue / month + net per $1 program + payback months) computed by `forecastLoyalty()` — same math as `playbooks/07-loyalty-program-smile.md`. Result is paste-ready markdown: copy-to-clipboard OR download `.md` (named `loyalty-launch-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.md`). 30 days, 4 weeks, 30 checkbox-able actions covering: app install + points/tiers/referral config + Klaviyo webhook wiring + Triple Whale cohort overlay (W1); 6-touch launch sequence build (3 emails + 3 SMS) + on-site widget + post-purchase + account-page embed + win-back flow for non-enrolled (W2); soft-launch to 10% then ramp to 50% / 100% + D-7 / D-14 / D-21 enrollment-rate readouts + support-team briefing (W3); 90-day repeat-rate proxy + payback-month readout + iteration backlog + Q2 priorities + 30-day program readout deck (W4). CTA button also surfaced on the Loyalty ROI calculator on `/playbooks/07-loyalty-program-smile` (next to "Reset defaults" and "Copy report") for at-handbook discovery. Sidebar nav entry added (icon ▦).

- **Why it matters:** Companion to the 3 existing launch-plan generators (PDP A/B, Welcome Series, Abandoned-Cart) — closes the same gap for the second-largest retention-lever program. Operators typically have the 3-tier VIP + 6-touch launch sequence template ready in Smile.io / Yotpo / LoyaltyLion but no calendar-paced checklist to drive the launch. The plan reads the operator's REAL existing-customer base / AOV / margin / enrollment-rate / expected-lift so a $500k DTC operator who hasn't tweaked the calc gets the plan generated from their real numbers, not the 5,000-customer / $75-AOV / 25%-baseline / +7-pts / 60%-enrollment / $249/mo Smile.io Growth / $60/mo overhead defaults. Cross-page intelligence: reads from both `loyalty-roi:v1` and `your-store:v1` so the snapshot is consistent across Overview, Playbooks, and the launch-plan route. The 90-day repeat-rate lift (+5 to +9 pts over baseline) is only achievable if the operator wires the Klaviyo + Postscript + Triple Whale + Smile stack in the right order; the plan enforces that ordering so the +5 pts lift isn't accidentally misattributed to the welcome series.

- **What shipped:** New route at `/checkout-audit-launch-plan` with a one-click "Generate 30-day launch plan" button. Opens a modal with a 30-day day-by-day checklist (Days 1–30 across W1–W4) generated from the operator's saved Baymard audit inputs (`ecom-ops:cro:checkout-audit:v1`). Snapshot block (current 0–100 Baymard score + health band + cumulative CVR-lift band, capped at +80%) computed by `scoreAudit()` — same math as `scripts/checkout_audit_score.py` + `dashboard/src/lib/checkout-audit.ts`. Result is paste-ready markdown: copy-to-clipboard OR download `.md` (named `checkout-audit-launch-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.md`). 30 days, 4 weeks, 30 checkbox-able actions covering: Severity L baseline + 5 highest-lift fixes (guest checkout, Shop Pay + Apple Pay + Google Pay, address autocomplete, single-page checkout, sticky place-order, real shipping cost upfront); Severity M fixes (minimum fields, inline validation, BNPL for AOV > $150, payment icons, trust badges, no guest redirect, touch-targets ≥44×44, 16px input fonts); Severity S polish (no password meter, visible field labels, inline errors, secure-checkout lock, returns-policy link, cross-browser audit); E5 real-device test + score-after-W3 + +CVR-lift proxy computation + Move #4 (mobile-PDP) cross-link + 30-day readout deck. CTA button also surfaced on `/cro` next to the Baymard audit card for at-handbook discovery. Sidebar nav entry added (icon ▦). The plan enforces W1 = Severity L only, so shipping the W1 plan alone moves the audit from weak/fair to good / great.

- **Why it matters:** Companion to the 9 existing launch-plan generators (PDP A/B #9.5, Welcome Series #3.4, Abandoned Cart #1, Loyalty #8, Post-Purchase Upsell #9.6, SMS-WC #6, Attribution-Alert #6.10, Subscription #11, 3PL #52) — closes the same gap for Move #3, the highest-CVR-leverage lever. The plan reads the operator's REAL audit state (current pass / partial / fail / skip / missing per guideline) so a $3M DTC operator who hasn't run the audit gets the plan generated from the missing-audit baseline (0/100 score, +80% CVR-lift ceiling), not industry placeholders. ## 2026-09-30 21:55 UTC — /master-rollout-calendar: 90-day multi-move Master Rollout Calendar generator + collision detection + .ics export (Move #N)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/master-rollout-calendar` with a one-click "Generate 90-day Master Rollout Calendar" button. Opens a modal that reads ALL 9 per-move calculator localStorage keys (`ecom-ops:playbooks:ac-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:ws-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:loyalty-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:ppu-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:sms-wc-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:pdp-ab:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:attribution-alert:v1` + `ecom-ops:subscription-path:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:threepl:v1` + `ecom-ops:cro:checkout-audit:v1`) plus `ecom-ops:your-store:v1`, sequences all 10 launches in canonical foundation → revenue → CRO → retention build order (Phase 1: SMS-WC + Welcome Series; Phase 2: Abandoned Cart + Post-Purchase Upsell; Phase 3: PDP A/B + Checkout Audit; Phase 4: Loyalty + Subscription + Attribution-Alert + 3PL), detects 3 kinds of collisions (klaviyo-sms-collision, klaviyo-email-collision, staff-constraint-collision), sums combined Year-1 net margin + cost across all 10 moves, computes combined ROI + health band. Result is a gantt-style 90-day markdown checklist + RFC 5545 .ics (one all-day event per move). Copy-to-clipboard + download `.md` + download `.ics`. Day-1 start date is operator-pickable (defaults to today); cross-tab sync via `storage` event so editing a calculator in another tab re-hydrates this calendar.

- **Why it matters:** Companion to the 9 existing launch-plan generators — closes the cross-move operational sequencing gap. The 9 per-move launch-plan generators each take the operator's per-move inputs and emit a 30-day markdown checklist. That works per-move, but the operator who has run 3-4 generators now has 60-120 days of un-sequenced work: what do they ship first? Which moves collide on Klaviyo / Postscript / SMS / ops in the same week? What's the combined Year-1 ROI? This page is the cross-move view: it walks the catalog in canonical build order (foundation first, retention last), detects same-week build collisions on Klaviyo / Klaviyo-SMS / staff-constraint with severity levels (info / warn / block), sums the per-move Year-1 net margin + cost into a combined ROI rollup (default Year-1 industry combined ROI ≈ 20:1 across the 10 moves, $895k net margin, $63k cost), and emits a single calendar-ready file the operator imports into Google Calendar / Apple Calendar / Outlook as colored all-day bands. Companion to `/30-day-plan` (single-move synthesis doc).

## 2026-10-01 05:30 UTC — /launch-plan-progress: cross-page-intelligence progress tracker for all 10 launch-plan generators (Move #N.2)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/launch-plan-progress` with an interactive 30-day × 10-plan grid tracker. Each of the 10 launch-plan pages (`/pdp-ab-launch-plan`, `/welcome-series-launch-plan`, `/abandoned-cart-launch-plan`, `/loyalty-launch-plan`, `/post-purchase-upsell-launch-plan`, `/sms-welcome-cart-launch-plan`, `/attribution-health-alert-launch-plan`, `/subscription-launch-plan`, `/3pl-launch-plan`, `/checkout-audit-launch-plan`) gets a per-plan card with: (a) clickable day cells (30 days per plan, click to mark shipped / un-shipped), (b) per-plan progress bar with W1/W2/W3/W4 completion counts, (c) health band ("complete" / "on-track" ≥60% / "started" 1–59% / "untouched" 0%), (d) first/last shipped date, (e) realised Year-1 net margin against the per-move default benchmark, (f) Reset button per plan. Top of page: aggregate rollup card (total days shipped, % completion, total realised Y1 margin, health band counts) + Copy/Download markdown buttons for the standup-ready rollup block. State persisted per-browser to `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:v1` (cross-tab sync via `storage` event; cross-component notify via custom `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:update` event).

- **Why it matters:** Closes the post-generation visibility gap for the 9 existing launch-plan generators. Operators today click "Generate" → get a markdown → paste into Linear / Notion / Slack → lose visibility into how many days they've actually shipped. This page is the operator-facing rollup: one tick box per action, one progress bar per plan, one aggregate card at the top. The realised-vs-default margin display makes the standup summary immediately CFO-readable (e.g. "$147,000 of $1,278,000 realised Y1 margin across the 10 plans = 11.5% shipped"). ## 2026-10-01 17:02 UTC — /launch-plan-progress: per-day ship notes overlay (Move #N.3)

- **What shipped:** New per-day ship notes overlay on `/launch-plan-progress`. Each shipped day cell now hosts an inline 280-char textarea; notes save to a new `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress-notes:v1` localStorage key (independent from the progress key, so un-ticking a day does NOT delete its note — operators keep notes for retros). Day cells display an amber corner-dot when a note exists and a hover-tooltip preview of the first 60 chars. Rollup header gained a 5th tile "Ship notes" (count + plans-annotated). New "Copy ship-notes rollup" + "Download notes .md" buttons emit a paste-ready markdown standup block: `# Launch-plan ship notes rollup` + per-plan H2 + `- **Day N** (YYYY-MM-DD): <note>` lines. Plan-row Reset button now clears notes for that plan too. Cross-tab sync via `storage` event for both keys; custom `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress-notes:update` event on every save; textarea autosaves on blur with green "Saved!" flash + chars-left counter.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the post-generation WHY gap for the 10 launch-plan generators. Operators tick Day 1 → "shipped" → but a standup reader needs the WHY (what shipped, what's blocked, who's owning the next step). Move #N.3 wires a per-day 280-char note (Twitter-length, Slack-message-friendly) so the standup rollup goes from `[X/Y days] PDP A/B Test launch plan — Move #9.5 — $realisedMargin / $defaultMargin` to `[X/Y days] PDP A/B Test launch plan — Move #9.5 — $realisedMargin / $defaultMargin` PLUS a chronological Day-by-Day narrative of WHY each shipped day shipped. Real operator use case: ticking Day 5 "Klaviyo flow live" with note "blocked: brand team held QA 2 days — design review passed Tuesday" gives the Monday standup the same context a real PM would put in Linear.

- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/launch-plan-progress — tick any day cell, type a note in the textarea that appears below it, click outside to save. The amber corner-dot + tooltip preview + new rollup tile + Copy/Download notes buttons are all live.

## 2026-10-02 02:30 UTC — /launch-plan-progress: per-day ship notes full-text search (Move #N.4)

- **What shipped:** New full-text search panel on `/launch-plan-progress`. Operators type a query (single term, multi-term AND-joined, or quoted phrase) and get ranked, highlighted results across every note attached to a ticked day on all 10 launch-plan pages. Each hit shows: plan title pill (links to the per-plan tracker), day number, shipped-date, match-count, and a context snippet with the matched substring wrapped in a `<mark>` highlight. Suggested-query chips (`blocked`, `Klaviyo`, `Shop Pay`, `"legal review"`, `pending`, `"brand team"`) populate the input for one-click common workflows. Copy/Download buttons emit a paste-ready markdown block (per-plan, per-day: `- **<title>** — Day N (YYYY-MM-DD): <note>`) for the matched subset.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the post-generation WHERE/WHO/WHAT gap for the 10 launch-plan generators. Operators ship days → attach notes ("Day 5 blocked: Klaviyo template QA held by brand team"). Within a few weeks the 280-char notes become a real corpus — and a standup reader or an incident responder needs to ask "find every 'blocked' mention", "find every note mentioning the brand lead", "every reference to Klaviyo across all 10 plans" in a single search. Move #N.4 wires a full-text search layer over the same localStorage map the notes overlay writes (`ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress-notes:v1` + cross-references `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:v1` to scope the index to actually-ticked days).

- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/launch-plan-progress — scroll to the new "Search ship notes" panel below the tracker. Type "blocked" or "Klaviyo" (or click a chip) and watch the result list render with amber `<mark>` highlights.
